name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican Chuck Gray's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Democratic nominee Lisa Kinney's minimal campaign resources
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~99%
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean makes this seat safely Republican even with Hageman retiring, and Gray holds an overwhelming money advantage over Kinney, who has raised under $20,000. Markets price a Republican win near certainty, so the forecast stays at a roughly twenty-point Republican margin.
model.watch: A major scandal or third-party surge could tighten the race, but nothing in the evidence suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is open this cycle as Republican Harriet Hageman leaves to run for Senate. Statewide official Chuck Gray enters as the Republican nominee with strong financial backing, having raised about $1.6 million with additional outside support. Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000, and minor-party candidates trail far behind.

The district's R+23 partisan lean and the lopsided resource gap make this a safe Republican hold. Prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 99 percent, and no polls or expert ratings point to a competitive race.
